---
title: "Link functions"
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

A **link function** maps a constrained conditional mean to the real-valued linear predictor. We continue with SuperTelicity, where the response is an *in* choice and the first-use source and design are introduced on the [preceding page](why-generalized-linear-models.qmd).

```{r}
#| label: load-and-fit-link
#| echo: true
st <- read.csv("data/supertelicity/supertelicity-cloze.csv")
st$verb_type <- factor(st$verb_type, levels = c("manner", "result"))
st$duration_centered <- st$log_duration_minutes -
  mean(st$log_duration_minutes, na.rm = TRUE)
st <- st[!is.na(st$duration_centered), ]
fit <- glm(prep_in ~ duration_centered + verb_type,
           family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = st)
```

For a Bernoulli mean $0<\pi_i<1$, the logit link and its inverse are

$$
g(\pi_i)=\log\frac{\pi_i}{1-\pi_i}=\eta_i,
\qquad
g^{-1}(\eta_i)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-\eta_i}}=\pi_i.
$$

The link acts on the conditional mean, not on the observed zeros and ones. The fitted SuperTelicity model supplies actual values on both scales.

```{r}
#| label: link-map
#| echo: true
observed <- aggregate(prep_in ~ verb_type, st, mean)
observed$empirical_logit <- qlogis(observed$prep_in)
observed$round_trip_probability <- plogis(observed$empirical_logit)
observed
```

`qlogis()` maps the empirical group probabilities to real numbers, and `plogis()` returns them to the probability scale. These functions implement the equations above without transforming any response row.

## The inverse link keeps predictions valid

```{r}
#| label: plot-link-fit
#| echo: true
library(ggplot2)
grid <- expand.grid(
  duration_centered = seq(min(st$duration_centered), max(st$duration_centered),
                          length.out = 201L),
  verb_type = levels(st$verb_type)
)
grid$log_duration_minutes <- grid$duration_centered + mean(st$log_duration_minutes)
grid$eta <- predict(fit, newdata = grid, type = "link")
grid$probability <- plogis(grid$eta)
st$duration_bin <- cut(st$log_duration_minutes,
  unique(quantile(st$log_duration_minutes, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 13L))),
  include.lowest = TRUE)
binned <- aggregate(cbind(prep_in, log_duration_minutes) ~ duration_bin + verb_type,
                    st, mean)
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = binned,
             aes(log_duration_minutes, prep_in, shape = verb_type), size = 1.7) +
  geom_line(data = grid,
            aes(log_duration_minutes, probability, linetype = verb_type),
            color = "#1F5A85", linewidth = .8) +
  labs(x = "Selected duration (log minutes)",
       y = "Probability of an in-completion", shape = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_classic()
```

The model is additive in $\eta_i$ but curved in $\pi_i$. A constant coefficient is a constant change in log odds, not in probability. The link changes neither the Bernoulli support nor the observed response. It connects the linear predictor to the family mean.

For count means the analogous construction uses $\log\lambda_i=\eta_i$ and $\lambda_i=e^{\eta_i}>0$. Thus the choice of link follows the support of the conditional mean. It is not a device for making a histogram look normal.
